takeoff_over_50ft_provenance.title: Performance Information - Landplane: Take-off Distance (Ft.), Flaps Up
takeoff_over_50ft_provenance.conditions: Flaps up, full throttle, to clear a 50 ft. obstacle at 76 MPH TIAS, gross weight 2200 lb, zero wind, hard surface level runway. The handbook prints only the total distance over the 50 ft obstacle; it gives the ground run as a rule rather than a column ("Ground run approx. 40% distance shown"), so no ground-roll value is carried. Distances are reduced approximately 10% for each 6 m.p.h. of wind.
takeoff_over_50ft_provenance.temperature_units: Columns are printed in degrees FAHRENHEIT (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 F) and carried at their exact Celsius equivalents.
takeoff_over_50ft_provenance.altitudes_published: Sea Level, 2000, 4000, 6000, 7000 ft; the 7000 ft row is not carried (see altitude_row_not_carried in this spec).
takeoff_over_50ft_provenance.note: The handbook also prints a flaps 20 deg take-off block and a note that 10 deg flap figures are approximately the same as 20 deg. That block is not carried (see figures_not_carried). Flaps up is the longer and therefore the conservative table.

source.doc: Cessna 170 Owner's Manual, "52, 53, 54 and 55 Models" (form P213-13-RPC-200-3/79). Section V - Operational Data, Performance Information - Landplane, printed page 37 (PDF page 43)
source.note: Exact variant: the cover reads "170 - 52, 53, 54 and 55 Models" and the MAIN DIFFERENCE TABLE on PDF page 4 lists the 1952-1955 model years with the Continental C-145-2 (1952-54) or O-300-A (1955) engine and 40 degree wing flaps. Those four model years are the 170B production run, so this book is the 170B handbook and nothing here is borrowed from the 1948 170 or the 1949-51 170A. Scanned book with no text layer at all (0 characters over 76 pages), so every number is read by macOS Vision OCR in overlapping strips (scripts/poh/ocr.py) and re-read by the verifier the same way. The whole performance section is one composite figure on printed page 37: four stacked blocks (landing distance flaps 40, take-off distance flaps up, take-off distance flaps 20, normal rate of climb) sharing one ALTITUDE column and one OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE header, so each block is read under its own clip. Conditions printed above the figure: "compiled from actual tests with airplane and engine in good condition and using average piloting technique. Data are based upon a gross weight of 2200 lbs. with McCauley propeller installed, and full throttle for take-off and climb. Performance figures are for zero wind velocity and hard surface level runway. Speeds are true indicated airspeeds." Footnote: "Both take-off and landing distances are reduced approximately 10% for each 6 m.p.h. wind velocity." TEMPERATURE UNITS: this handbook prints its temperature axis in DEGREES FAHRENHEIT (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 F). The pipeline's row key is oat_c, so each column is carried at its exact Celsius equivalent (-17.8, -6.7, 4.4, 15.6, 26.7, 37.8 C) rather than at its Fahrenheit face value. No value is interpolated or shifted; only the column label is converted. ALTITUDE AXIS: the figure prints Sea Level, 2000, 4000, 6000 and 7000 ft, but only the first four rows are carried. See altitude_row_not_carried below.

landing_over_50ft_provenance.title: Performance Information - Landplane: Landing Distance (Ft.), Flaps 40 deg
landing_over_50ft_provenance.conditions: Flaps 40 deg, to land over a 50 ft. obstacle at 67 MPH TIAS approach, gross weight 2200 lb, zero wind, hard surface level runway. The handbook prints only the total distance over the 50 ft obstacle; it gives the ground roll as a rule rather than a column ("Roll 40% distance shown"), so no ground-roll value is carried. Distances are reduced approximately 10% for each 6 m.p.h. of wind.
landing_over_50ft_provenance.temperature_units: Columns are printed in degrees FAHRENHEIT (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 F) and carried at their exact Celsius equivalents.
landing_over_50ft_provenance.altitudes_published: Sea Level, 2000, 4000, 6000, 7000 ft; the 7000 ft row is not carried (see altitude_row_not_carried in this spec).

rate_of_climb_provenance.title: Performance Information - Landplane: Normal Rate of Climb, Feet per min., Flaps Up
rate_of_climb_provenance.conditions: Flaps up, full throttle, gross weight 2200 lb, McCauley propeller. Best climb speed TIAS is printed beside the rows and is not carried as a field because it sits LEFT of the altitude column, outside the window the shared extractor reads: 89 MPH at sea level, 86 at 2000 ft, 84 at 4000 ft, 81 at 6000 ft, 79 at 7000 ft.
